title: Timber for Godot 4 is live: 48 ways to chop down the trees you already painted
html:
Timber is live for Godot 4: the trees already painted on your TileMapLayer become trees your players can chop down. 48 fell styles, 6 kinds of tree by 8 falls, and every chip, leaf, log and stump is drawn by code from the pixels of the tree itself.

What it does

  • Tag your tree tiles with one custom data word. TimberLayer2D finds each tree however you painted it: one big atlas tile, several tiles painted together, or a trunk with its canopy on a second layer.
  • Each blow shudders the tree and opens a notch in its own bark. The last one brings it down: it topples, crashes, snaps at the notch, whips over, tips out roots and all, slides off a clean cut, bursts where it stands or burns from the foot up.
  • The crown breaks into clumps of its own leaves, the trunk splits into logs cut from its own bark, a stump stays and blocks like the trunk did, and later a sapling grows back and the exact cells return.
  • Signals for a blow, a fall, a landing and every log, so your game can hand out wood. Saves keep felled trees as stumps.

Tested

  • Every style photographed under Forward+ and Compatibility: 96 frames, zero engine errors, all 48 distinct.
  • The shipped zip installed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project under both renderers: six trees painted three ways, all felled, every cell put back exactly on regrowth, a save loaded into a fresh level, and a whip felled left and right measured as mirror images.
  • 7 attacks, including a path with spaces and non Latin characters, fifty trees felled in the same frame, a third renderer, bad inputs and a renamed addon folder; 216 Readme claims checked against the shipped files.
  • Looking at the pictures found what no counter could. A root ball drew as an open fan, three palm falls were one picture because every palm bent, a whip bent its crown the wrong way when it fell to the left, and a bent crown came apart in stripes. The gate passed all of them. All were fixed before release.

Free lite

The page carries a free MIT lite: 12 of the 48 styles (topple and crash on every kind), the same nodes, and a demo.

Where this line stands: 24 Godot packs live from this studio, 3 purchases so far (read from the store the day this went live).

Disclosure: the scripts and demo were written with AI; the demo trees come from our own generated tilesets and the cover illustration was made by an AI image model.
